title: Adding endings: doubling, dropping and changing y
subject: LANGUAGE

slides.title: Adding -ing and -ly
slides.text:
We add endings to words.

play → play**ing**
quick → quick**ly**

Most of the time, we just **add** the ending.

slides.title: Drop the silent e
slides.text:
If a word ends in a **silent e**, drop the e before **-ing**.

make → **making**
ride → **riding**
write → **writing**

slides.title: Short words, one vowel
slides.text:
If a short word ends in **one vowel + one consonant**, double the last letter before -ing.

run → ru**nn**ing
sit → si**tt**ing
swim → swi**mm**ing

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Look at the base word. Does it end in **e**?
2. Find other -ing words in the text.
3. See how they changed. Use the same rule.

example.explain:
bake → **baking** (drop e)
smile → **smiling** (drop e)
play → **playing** (just add -ing)

together.passage: It is Friday morning. Grandma is ___ bread in the kitchen. My sister is riding her bike in the yard. I am writing a card for Grandma.
together.hint: **make** ends in a silent e. What do you do with the e before -ing?

sentences: Grandma is ___ bread in the kitchen.
My sister is riding her bike in the yard.
I am writing a card for Grandma.
evidence.stem: The answer was: making. Tap 2 sentences with other words that dropped the e before -ing.
evidence.wrong: This sentence has no word that dropped an e. Look again.

checks.passage: The dog ran ___ across the yard.
The children are ___ in the pool.
checks.why: **swim** has one vowel and ends in one consonant, so double the **m**: **swimming**.

checks.passage: Huda is ___ a picture of a camel.
checks.why: **draw** does not end in e, so just add **-ing**: **drawing**.

again.title: Look at the last letter
again.text:
Before you add -ing, look at the **last letter**.

**e**? Drop it.
**one vowel + one consonant** in a short word? Double it.
Anything else? Just add -ing.

slides.title: Words ending in y
slides.text:
When a word ends in **consonant + y**, change the **y** to **i** before most endings.

happy → happ**i**ly, happ**i**ness
carry → carr**i**ed
cry → cr**i**es

slides.title: Keep y before -ing
slides.text:
Do **not** change the y before **-ing**. That would make two i's.

carry → carr**y**ing
cry → cr**y**ing
study → stud**y**ing

slides.title: Vowel + y stays
slides.text:
When a **vowel** comes before the y, keep the y.

play → pla**y**ed
enjoy → enjo**y**ment
stay → sta**y**s

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Look at the letter **before** the y.
2. Consonant → change y to i (but not before -ing). Vowel → keep the y.
3. Find other words in the text that follow the same rule.

sentences.t: The puppy hurried to its bowl.
It was hungry, so it ate greedily.
Then it played with a ball.

example.explain:
hurry → **hurried**, greedy → **greedily**: consonant + y, so y changes to i.

play → **played**: vowel + y, so the y stays.

together.passage: Last week, my little cousin stayed with us. On the first night, she ___ because she missed her mother. My mom carried her around the house and sang softly. The next morning, she happily drew pictures with my old crayons. By the end of the week, she was the happiest girl in our house.
together.hint: **cry** ends in consonant + y. What happens to the y before -ed?

sentences: Last week, my little cousin stayed with us.
On the first night, she ___ because she missed her mother.
My mom carried her around the house and sang softly.
The next morning, she happily drew pictures with my old crayons.
By the end of the week, she was the happiest girl in our house.
evidence.stem: The answer was: cried. Tap 2 sentences with other words where y changed to i.
evidence.wrong: Here the y stays (a vowel comes before it), or no word changes y. Look for words where y became i.

checks.passage: My little brother is ___ his toys to his room.
We ___ our trip to the beach.
checks.why: **enjoy** has a vowel before the y, so keep the y: **enjoyed**.

checks.passage: The old man walked ___ up the hill.
checks.why: **slow** + **ly** = **slowly**. There is no y to change.

again.title: Ask about the neighbour
again.text:
Look at the letter right before the **y**.

Is it a, e, i, o or u? → keep the y.
Is it any other letter? → change y to i (except before -ing).
again.example:
pay → pa**y**ing, pa**y**ment (a before y)
busy → bus**i**ly, bus**i**ness (s before y)

slides.title: The doubling rule
slides.text:
In a **one-syllable** word that ends in **one vowel + one consonant**, double the last consonant before an ending that starts with a vowel (-ing, -ed, -er, -est).

stop → sto**pp**ed
plan → pla**nn**ing
big → bi**gg**est

slides.title: When not to double
slides.text:
Do **not** double when:

1. There are **two vowels** before the last letter: rain → rai**n**ing
2. The word ends in **two consonants**: jump → jum**p**ed
3. The ending starts with a **consonant**: sad → sa**d**ness, glad → gla**d**ly

slides.title: Never double w, x, y
slides.text:
The letters **w**, **x** and **y** are never doubled.

fix → fi**x**ed
snow → sno**w**ing
play → pla**y**er

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Count the vowels before the last letter.
2. Count the consonants at the end.
3. Check: does the ending start with a vowel?

Find other words in the passage with doubled letters, and words without. See which rule each one follows.

sentences.t: The runner slipped on the wet track.
Then he waited for the next race.

example.explain:
slip → **slipped**: one vowel + one consonant, so double.
jump → **jumped**: two consonants at the end, no doubling.
wait → **waited**: two vowels, no doubling.

together.passage: On Saturday, my father and I planned a fishing trip. We got up early and packed our bags. On the way to the coast, the car ___ at a small shop so we could buy bait. At the beach, I was hopping from rock to rock while Dad was setting up the rods. By noon, we had caught three fish, and the sun was getting hotter.
together.hint: **stop** has one vowel and ends in one consonant. The ending **-ed** starts with a vowel.

sentences: On Saturday, my father and I planned a fishing trip.
We got up early and packed our bags.
On the way to the coast, the car ___ at a small shop so we could buy bait.
At the beach, I was hopping from rock to rock while Dad was setting up the rods.
By noon, we had caught three fish, and the sun was getting hotter.
evidence.stem: The answer was: stopped. Tap 2 sentences with other words that double the last consonant before an ending.
evidence.wrong: No consonant is doubled here. The base words end in two consonants or have no ending added.

checks.passage: Our team is ___ to win the match.
checks.why: **plan** has one vowel and one consonant at the end, so double the **n**: **planning**.

checks.passage: It was ___ all afternoon, so we stayed inside.
checks.why: **rain** has **two vowels** before the n, so do not double: **raining**.

checks.passage: The ___ boy in our class is Faisal.
checks.why: **tall** already ends in two consonants. Just add **-est**: **tallest**.

again.title: 1-1-1 check
again.text:
Double the last letter only if the word has:

**1** syllable
**1** vowel before the last letter
**1** consonant at the end

and the ending starts with a vowel.
again.example:
hot → 1-1-1 → ho**tt**er ✔
heat → two vowels → hea**t**er ✘ (no doubling)
help → two consonants → hel**p**er ✘

slides.title: Longer words
slides.text:
For words with **two or more syllables**, double the final consonant only if the **stress** is on the **last** syllable.

be**GIN** → begi**nn**ing
pre**FER** → prefe**rr**ed
ad**MIT** → admi**tt**ed

slides.title: Stress at the start
slides.text:
If the stress is on an **earlier** syllable, do **not** double.

**VIS**it → visi**t**ed
**O**pen → ope**n**ing
**HAP**pen → happe**n**ed

Say the word aloud and listen for the strong beat.

slides.title: Tricky -ly words
slides.text:
Some words change before **-ly**:

true → **truly** (drop e)
gentle → **gently** (drop le, add ly)
full → **fully** (just add y)
day → **daily** (y to i, even after a vowel)

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Say the base word aloud. Where is the stress?
2. Last syllable stressed + one vowel + one consonant → double.
3. Compare with other words in the passage. Notice which ones doubled and which did not, and listen for the stress in each.

sentences.t: The game was about to begin.
At the beginning, our team was nervous.
Then we opened the scoring with a great goal.

example.explain:
be**GIN**: stress on the last syllable → **beginning**.

**O**pen: stress on the first syllable → **opened**, no doubling.

together.passage: At the ___ of the school year, our class started a reading challenge. Each of us committed to reading twenty books. I preferred adventure stories, while my friend Huda chose books about history. Our teacher visited the library with us every week and listened to our reviews. By June, we had truly passed our goal, and the principal admitted she was impressed.
together.hint: Say **begin** aloud. Which syllable is stressed?
together.good: Yes! The stress is on **-GIN**, so double the **n**: **beginning**.

sentences: At the ___ of the school year, our class started a reading challenge.
Each of us committed to reading twenty books.
I preferred adventure stories, while my friend Huda chose books about history.
Our teacher visited the library with us every week and listened to our reviews.
By June, we had truly passed our goal, and the principal admitted she was impressed.
evidence.stem: The answer was: beginning. Tap 2 sentences with other two-syllable words that double the final consonant.
evidence.wrong: The words here are stressed on the first syllable, so they do not double. Find words stressed at the end.

checks.passage: Our neighbours ___ us to their new home for dinner.
checks.why: **invite** ends in a silent e. Drop it and add **-ed**: **invited**.
**HAP**pen is stressed on the first syllable, so do not double: **happened**.
For words ending in **-le**, drop the **le** and add **-ly**: **gently**.

again.title: Clap the beat
again.text:
Clap the syllables and say the word.

Strong clap at the **end**? Double before -ing or -ed.
Strong clap at the **start**? Just add the ending.
